digest.component_or_area: tickets-branch push delivery on async, library, and MCP paths
propositions: A failed tickets-branch push on the async path (sync.push=async) creates a detached Popen with stderr=DEVNULL and start_new_session=True, so all warning output is discarded by the OS and the failure is invisible to the caller.

Library embedders calling rebar.comment(...) see no push failure signal because rebar/__init__.py attaches a NullHandler and install_stderr_handler runs only from CLI/MCP, so stderr remains empty even when a real push was rejected.

MCP write tools (comment_ticket, etc.) return {result: ok} to the agent even when the push was rejected by the remote, because the handler targets the server's stderr which the agent never reads, leaving commits stranded invisibly.
The reconciler subprocess's push is mute because it installs its handler on the rebar_reconciler root while rebar._store.push logs under rebar, so rejections are invisible even in the foreground.

Every terminal failure funnels through _raise_if_strict() which must record a durable marker to the git dir (not working tree, to preserve git status invariant) naming the failure reason, recorded regardless of logging handler installation.

A durable pending/unpushed marker in the git dir enables mute paths (async, library, MCP) to report push failures via rebar.push_status() and a push_status field on MCP write-tool results without changing exit codes or raising exceptions.
